pages: 5594275-UIM-B-1020 Section I: General information The Hx™3 Zone Control Module kit is for use in a multi-zone HVAC system. Multi-zone systems can save energy and provide optimum comfort in a site. The kit includes the Hx 3 Zone Control Module and the leaving air sensor. The main function of the Hx 3 Zone Control Module is to communicate with the Hx™3 Touch Screen Thermostat acting as the Main Control in the zoning system, and provide 24 VAC outputs to the zone dampers. The purpose of this document is to do the following: • Explain how to install and use the Hx 3 Zone Control Module, and how it operates within the zoning system. • Provide information on the wider zoning system, including a procedure for zoning system installation. For more information on specific zoning components and indoor and outdoor equipment, refer to the associated documentation. The zoning system can include different zoning components, depending on the requirements of a site and the number of zones. Components have specific names in the zoning software. Table 1 provides an overview. The product naming used throughout this document reflects Table 1. Table 1: Zoning components Component Function Name in zoning software Notes Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostat (S1-THXU430W) Act as Main Control (zone 1) Act as zone thermostat sensor in zones 2–8 Main Control Zone Thermostat-Hx You must use a Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostat as the Main Control for zoning operation. You can use additional Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostats as zone thermostats in zones 2–8 as required. Understand and pay particular attention to the signal words DANGER, WARNING, and CAUTION. DANGER indicates an imminently hazardous situation, which, if not avoided, will result in death or serious injury. WARNING indicates a potentially hazardous situation, which, if not avoided, could result in death or serious injury. This product does not support direct connection with pneumatic dampers. Use 24 VAC three-wire power open/power close dampers. NOTICE The indoor unit must be capable of communications. Use of the communicating interface control (S1-33102953000) is not supported with zoning. Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostat software requirements You must use a Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostat as the Main Control. For easy installation, use Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostats as the Main Control and zone thermostats (for zones 2–8) on the zoning system. It is best practice to update the thermostat software from non-zoning software to zoning software (02.00 or greater) before installation. Verify the software version shown on the outside of the thermostat box as shown in the following figure: A1136-001 Figure 1: Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostat box label IMPORTANT: Confirm the software version on the outside label of the Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostat box: • When the thermostat is installed as the Main Control, the software version must be greater than 01.11 to support zoning operation. • When the thermostat is installed as a zone thermostat, the software version must be greater than 02.00 to support zoning operation. 5594275-UIM-B-1020 Wiring ! WARNING ELECTRICAL OPERATION HAZARD Failure to follow this warning could result in personal injury, death, or equipment damage. Before installing, modifying, or servicing the system, the main electrical disconnect switch must be in the Off position. There may be more than one switch with a suitable warning label. Wiring requirements All wiring must comply with local electrical codes and ordinances. Use standard 18 AWG (solid) copper thermostat wires to connect the communicating system. Special (shielded) cable is not generally required. As with all communicating devices, it is best practice to keep wiring at least 1 ft away from large inductive loads. Examples of large inductive loads include electronic air cleaners, high voltage wiring, florescent light ballasts, LED lighting, and motors. If you do not adhere to these wiring practices, electrical interference (noise) may be introduced. Electrical interference may cause erratic system operation. NOTICE There may be installation applications where large inductive loads cannot be avoided. In these cases, use shielded wire to ensure proper system functionality. System wiring overview IMPORTANT: The communicating system requires four wires to operate. Ensure to supply at least four wires to each component of the zoning system. The communicating system is connected by four wires. Two of the wires are used to bring power to the individual zoning components (R and C), and three of the wires are used for serial communication (A+, C, and B-). Note: For variable capacity outdoor equipment applications, do not connect the indoor 24 VAC R connection to the outdoor equipment. Johnson Controls Ducted Systems 15

5594275-UIM-B-1020 Main Control wiring (zone 1) Connect the Hx 3 Touch Screen Thermostat acting as the Main Control to the four-wire screw terminals in Quadrant E (*MAIN CTRL) in the lower right corner of the Primary Zone Module. Note: See Figure 4 for wiring connections. NOTICE If more than one zone thermostat is connected to the zone system, replace the indoor equipment 40 VA transformer with a 75 VA transformer. Zone sensor wiring (zones 2–8) Connect the communicating zone sensors to the four-wire screw terminals in Quadrant A (ZONE SENSORS) on the left side of the Hx 3 Zone Control Module. Note the following: • Use the Primary Zone Module for zones 2–4. • Use the Secondary Zone Module for zones 5–8 if applicable. Note: See Figure 5 for wiring connections. NOTICE For ease of system configuration and troubleshooting, it is best practice to connect each zone thermostat and/or sensor to the zone number that corresponds to the number assigned to the zone in which it is located. Connect the zone 1 thermostat to the four-wire terminal labeled MAIN CONTROL. Zone thermostats and/or zone sensors (zones 2–8) function properly when connected to any of the four-wire terminals labeled ZONE SENSORS. Indoor and outdoor equipment wiring Connect the communicating indoor equipment (furnace or air handler) and communicating outdoor equipment (air conditioner or heat pump) to the Primary Zone Module using the four-wire screw terminals in Quadrant D (*HVAC EQUIPMENT). The indoor equipment transformer provides 24 VAC power to the Hx 3 Zone Control Module and all of the zone sensors, as well as the outdoor equipment and accessory controls. Variable capacity outdoor equipment does not have an R connection. Notes: Do not connect the R wire from the *HVAC EQUIPMENT terminal in Quadrant D to variable capacity outdoor equipment. See Figure 4 for wiring connections. IMPORTANT: If a modulating furnace is being used as the indoor HVAC equipment, place the ZONE CONTROL jumper in the Yes position. See Figure 10 for the jumper location. Zone control jumper A1360-001 Figure 10: Zone control jumper - modulating furnace Damper wiring Connect the zone dampers (purchased separately) to the appropriate three-wire zone damper output screw terminals in Quadrant C (ZONE DAMPERS) of the Hx 3 Zone Control Module. Note the following: • Use the Primary Zone Module for zones 1–4. • Use the Secondary Zone Module for zones 5–8 if applicable. 5594275-UIM-B-1020 ! WARNING Hx 3 ZONE CONTROL MODULE DAMPER WIRE HAZARD The Hx 3 Zone Control Module is designed to wire a maximum of five (24 VAC) three-wire dampers in parallel, per damper output. Failure to follow this warning could result in personal injury or damage to the Hx 3 Zone Control Module. NOTICE Connect the zone dampers to the appropriate zone number as specified before performing the auto setup process on the Main Control. Use the Restore defaults table in the Quick Reference Guide included in the Hx 3 Zone Control Module kit to record installer settings.
